### The Account

**The Number, Three Ways:** The plan's own commits (`e4d615f51` through `0d686c2e9`, twenty-one in all) sum to **+45 Actionable lines** (code minus comments; tests and documents excluded), measured one commit at a time: Phases 1 to 5 removed 149, Phases 6 to 8 added 142, and the final verification's three rounds added 52 (the simplification round took 16 away; the owner's ruling that nothing is carried and the neutral reviewer's corrections put 68 back as fixes). The table above counts the whole range `abfbf0798..0d686c2e9`, which also holds the Text Color plan's three commits and two unrelated ones in overlapping files, so its figures are not this plan's alone. The neutral reviewer, counting independently, read the whole range at +88 production lines, the link work alone at about +39, and about flat once comment lines are discounted. Tests went from 7919 to 8042 passing, some of them the peer work's. The −100 goal was not met; the owner ruled on 10-16-2026 that the floor is the goal rather than a gate, and this section is the account beside the count.

**What Collapsed, Layer by Layer:** Counted as ways of doing one thing before and after, re-tallied from the landed code: 93 ways of doing thirty things became 35.

- **Grammar:** two markdown link patterns became one; two link occurrence shapes (different fields per syntax) became one; three places splitting a destination at `#` became one; three `[label](dest)` templates became one; two default-label spellings became one; four local span types became one. After the verification, the grammar also owns its three fast gates ("could this text hold a link, name a heading, name this document's own heading"), which were spelled in five places.
- **Readers:** three whole-link readers became one; two resolvers became one, holding the page-before-address and bare-heading rules once where four places applied them; five "which slot holds the caret" tests became one; two owners of the raw-HTML question became one; five editor caret readers became four over one line walk. The verification found a fourth owner of "read a slot as a name" in the rename rewriter, which decoded a markdown destination but never stripped `.md`, so `[Notes](Notes.md)` renamed to Alpha kept its stale label; it reads through the one reader now.
- **Walk and index:** two tree walks became one; two title indexes became one that both processes import; the host interface that spread the index across itself is gone; two path-to-id maps became one; three duplicate-id policies became two, one for showing and one for writing, each stated.
- **Tracker:** four trackers of an edit inside a link became one; three Remove Title decisions became one rule, asked once by the picker and paste alike (the two had spelled the baseline fold in full).
- **Picker:** eleven query vocabulary items (seven form names, three predicates, a closer switch) became two axes and one record; eight commit arms became three; two closer tables became one, the grammar's.
- **Rules and writer:** three spellings of "does the shown text name the target" became one; two slot checks became one; four writers bypassing the markdown fallback became one (a File reference, by ruling); two rename carry-and-drop implementations became one serving both arms; two shown-text spellings became one behind sort, filter, and Remove Link.
- **Index facts:** two frontmatter value readers became one; two keys rules became one, applied by the graph, the cascade, and the Spaces check with the registry in memory (the disk read beside it is gone); two relation kinds a value link could land in became one row under its key; the write-only count column is gone.
- **Fields:** three Link and Text field editors became one value editor; two Link Rename writers became one; two popover chromes became one; the alias list's key sniff is gone.

Counted as named things from the plan's Concepts tables as landed: 95 removed, 88 added, 7 fewer.

**What the Ruled Behaviors Cost, and What They Fixed:** The three phases that added lines, and the verification, each bought something named.

- **Phase 6, the rules and the one writer (+52):** a heading renamed or picked into text a wikilink can't spell now falls back to the markdown form instead of going stale or splitting the link; a table cell's pipe is escaped by the one writer; Text values sort and filter on what they show; paste writes a page-held address as that page; three wrong results from the copies disagreeing were made right.
- **Phase 7, index facts (+15):** every link in a frontmatter value is one row under its key, judged at read with the registry in hand, so creating a property over a held key changes the graph with no re-index, and a Number key no longer shadows a Link key.
- **Phase 8, one editor surface (+75):** every place a connection is typed is the same editor with the picker, the tracker, and alias memory, keeping a plain field's feel; a cancelled edit is terminal; an unchanged value never writes.
- **The verification (+52 net):** a markdown label the grammar couldn't read back (256 characters, or a leading caret) no longer turns a link into plain text through the rename cascade, the picker, or the settle; a heading re-pick obeys Remove Title as a title re-pick does; a cancelled Text field no longer remembers an alias from an edit it discarded; the cascade reads the registry in memory everywhere, closing a narrow race and dropping a disk read per rename; the Paste As rows resolve a page-held address through the host's index; the label's escapes are hidden on screen in the editor and the resting cell as the brackets are.

**What Grew Beyond the Estimates, and Why:** The estimates priced each one-line rule at one line; under the formatter most wrap to three, which is where Phase 6's band was missed. Phase 8's one-line lifecycle (the break filter, the invalid state, the blur, the key split, the seat) formats to twice its sketch. The verification's additions are the memory queue for the Text field (+13), the Paste As index plumbing (+10), the derived id and path maps (+10), and the resting cell hiding escapes by position through nested tokens (+20). Comments grew by about 45 lines net, each where a reader meets a rule or an exception. Nothing that arrived is a second way of doing something that already had one.

**Closed Rather Than Fixed, With Reasons:** the Matrix's two dedupes collapse different things on either side of the bridge; the entity record carries the icon the renderer's glyphs need and the persisted baseline keeps its four fields by its own contract; the open-slot holder keeps one grammar where the before kept two; the show and write id policies are deliberate and cross-cited; the sort extracts its key once per row; a resting-cell click inside an escaped label seats at the link's edge as the `Title § Heading` join already does; a title-cache entry persisted under a scheme-less spelling fetches once more; an HTML tag inside a markdown label draws its own text; the heading-rename settle has thirty direct tests; a pick into an unclosed link keeps the slot's remainder as prose; the tile handle's pick tree and the move targets build different products; `linkTokenAt` filters cached tokens where `linkAt` walks text; the plain-links setting is one root class; `readPageRelations`' `key` names the same concept as `Relation.key`.

**Awaiting the Owner's Eyes:** the fields' feel; the Text pane and the one-line field after the height chain moved to the page editor; the Number popover's content-sized width; the Link popover re-measuring after its bloom; Rename on an address value; a Link field's tint; an escaped label (`[a\]b](Page)`) drawn in a resting table cell; a heading re-pick with Remove Title On Link Change on; Escape in a one-line Text field after typing an alias. The content index moved to generation 15, so the running instance reindexes NexusOS once on its next open.

```/Core/MarkdownPM/Links/linkSettle.ts diff
+import { type EditorView, ViewPlugin, type ViewUpdate } from '@codemirror/view'
+import {
+  type ChangeSpec,
+  type EditorState,
+  type Line,
+  MapMode,
+  StateEffect,
+  StateField,
+  type Transaction,
+} from '@codemirror/state'
+import { escapeLabel, fitsSlot } from '../../Connections/links'
+import { type LinkOccurrence, targetSpan } from '../../Connections/connections'
+import {
+  keepsShown,
+  type LinkTarget,
+  pageLabel,
+  readLinkText,
+  readOccurrence,
+  resolveLink,
+  shownAlias,
+} from '../../Connections/linkValue'
+import type { PageIndex } from '../../Connections/pageIndex'
+import type { MarkdownScope } from '../Engine/detect'
+import type { Span } from '../Engine/markdownCode'
+import { docScan } from '../docCache'
+import { linkAt, linkWithin } from '../Input/edits'
+import { editorHost, inRawHtml } from '../api'
+import { inCaretPane } from '../Menus/caretPane'
+import { linkRest, restedOnLink } from './linkReveal'
+
+// The link an edit is being made inside, from the change that arms it to the settle that remembers its alias and collapses its emptied parts.
+
+interface Writing {
+  start: number
+  was: string
+}
+
+type Remembered = NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof shownAlias>>
+
+export const linkSettled = StateEffect.define<null>()
+
+/** The link an edit is being made inside, as it read before the first edit: what the typing color, alias memory, emptied-part collapse, and the Remove Title baseline all compare against. Armed by a typed or deleted change reaching into a link, mapped through changes, dropped with its opener, cleared when the settle lands. */
+export const linkWriting = StateField.define<Writing | null>({
+  create: () => null,
+  update(w, tr) {
+    if (tr.effects.some((e) => e.is(linkSettled))) return null
+    if (!tr.docChanged) return w
+    const edited = tr.isUserEvent('input') || tr.isUserEvent('delete')
+    if (!w) return edited ? changedLink(tr, null) : null
+    const start = tr.changes.mapPos(w.start, 1)
+    const kept = start === w.start ? w : { start, was: w.was }
+    const relinked = edited ? changedLink(tr, kept) : null
+    return relinked ?? (tr.changes.mapPos(w.start, 1, MapMode.TrackAfter) === null ? null : kept)
+  },
+})
+
+/** How the link at `start` read before the edit being made inside it began, else as it reads now; `now` is null for a link that never closed. */
+function baselineAt(state: EditorState, start: number, now: string | null): string | null {
+  const w = state.field(linkWriting, false)
+  return w?.start === start ? w.was : now
+}
+
+/** Whether re-aiming the link at `start` to `next` keeps its shown text: `keepsShown` asked against the link's baseline where `state` holds one, and against `now` for a surface without an editor state. */
+export function keptShown(
+  state: EditorState | null,
+  start: number,
+  now: string | null,
+  next: LinkTarget,
+  removeTitle: boolean,
+  index?: PageIndex,
+): boolean {
+  const was = state ? baselineAt(state, start, now) : now
+  return keepsShown(was === null ? null : readLinkText(was), next, removeTitle, index)
+}
+
+// The link already armed keeps its baseline, a replace over the whole of it included; only a change landing in another link reads the old document for how that link read.
+function changedLink(tr: Transaction, kept: Writing | null): Writing | null {
+  const scan = docScan.after(tr)
+  let found: Writing | null = null
+  tr.changes.iterChangedRanges((fromA, toA, fromB, toB) => {
+    if (found) return
+    const after = linkWithin(scan, fromB, toB)
+    if (!after) return
+    found =
+      after.start === kept?.start
+        ? kept
+        : {
+            start: after.start,
+            was: linkWithin(docScan(tr.startState.doc), fromA, toA)?.text ?? '',
+          }
+  })
+  return found
+}
+
+/** The link starting exactly at `start`, with its line. */
+function linkStartingAt(
+  state: EditorState,
+  start: number,
+): { line: Line; o: LinkOccurrence } | null {
+  const line = state.doc.lineAt(start)
+  const o = linkAt(docScan(state.doc), start + 1)
+  return o && line.from + o.full[0] === start ? { line, o } : null
+}
+
+/** Every empty part of the link at `start`: an empty alias takes its pipe and an empty heading its hash, matching the nexus-wide rule that an emptied value drops its key; a markdown link can't drop its label, so an empty one shows the label the draw gives it, as a picked one does, and an emptied address label stays empty, since an address has none. */
+function emptied(state: EditorState, start: number): ChangeSpec[] {
+  const hit = linkStartingAt(state, start)
+  if (!hit) return []
+  const { line, o } = hit
+  const empty = (s: Span | null): s is Span => s !== null && s[0] === s[1]
+  if (o.syntax === 'wiki')
+    return [
+      ...(empty(o.heading)
+        ? [{ from: line.from + o.heading[0] - 1, to: line.from + o.heading[1] }]
+        : []),
+      ...(empty(o.shown)
+        ? [{ from: line.from + targetSpan(o)[1], to: line.from + o.shown[1] }]
+        : []),
+    ]
+  if (!empty(o.shown)) return []
+  const written = readOccurrence(line.text, o)
+  const index = state.facet(editorHost).connections()?.index
+  const label = pageLabel(written, resolveLink(written, index))
+  return label && fitsSlot(label)
+    ? [{ from: line.from + o.shown[0], insert: escapeLabel(label) }]
+    : []
+}
+
+/** When a surface's alias memory writes: `leave` as the caret leaves the link, `flush` once its host flushes, so a field whose edit can be cancelled remembers only what it saved, and `never` where the surface's write layer remembers. */
+export type Remembers = 'leave' | 'flush' | 'never'
+
+/** A body reaches the memory only where a link is written, typed into or picked, either syntax, and it remembers once the caret leaves that link, against how the link read before, since a scan of bodies can't honor a real forget; under `flush` what the leave would write queues until the host's `flush`, and an unmount without one drops it. Its emptied parts collapse at the leave too, so reading a note never rewrites it and clearing a slot to retype never pulls the pipe from under the caret: the collapse is deferred and stands down if the caret is back in the link when it runs. The field clears only when the collapse lands, so `settling` holds the link already being settled and a second leave of it before then settles nothing. Blur settles on the event and unmount through `flush`, since the editor's own teardown outruns a deferred dispatch. */
+export const linkSettle = ViewPlugin.define(
+  (view: EditorView, { scope, remembers }: { scope: MarkdownScope; remembers: Remembers }) => {
+    let settling: number | null = null
+    const queued: Remembered[] = []
+    const holds = (start: number): boolean =>
+      view.hasFocus &&
+      linkWithin(docScan(view.state.doc), view.state.selection.main.head)?.start === start
+    const write = ({ page, alias }: Remembered): void =>
+      void view.state.facet(editorHost).aliases.edit(page.id, { op: 'add', alias })
+    const remember = (w: Writing): void => {
+      const api = view.state.facet(editorHost).connections()
+      const hit = linkStartingAt(view.state, w.start)
+      const shown =
+        hit && api ? shownAlias(hit.line.text.slice(...hit.o.full), api.index, w.was) : null
+      if (!shown) return
+      if (remembers === 'flush') queued.push(shown)
+      else write(shown)
+    }
+    const settle = (w: Writing, defer: boolean): void => {
+      if (settling === w.start && defer) return
+      const html = inRawHtml(view.state, w.start, scope)
+      if (settling !== w.start && !html && remembers !== 'never') remember(w)
+      settling = w.start
+      const collapse = (): void => {
+        if (settling === w.start) settling = null
+        if (defer && holds(w.start)) return
+        const armed = view.state.field(linkWriting)?.start === w.start
+        const changes = view.state.changes(html ? [] : emptied(view.state, w.start))
+        const rest = view.state.field(linkRest)
+        view.dispatch({
+          changes,
+          effects: [
+            ...(armed ? [linkSettled.of(null)] : []),
+            ...(rest === null ? [] : [restedOnLink.of(changes.mapPos(rest, 1))]),
+          ],
+        })
+      }
+      if (defer) setTimeout(collapse, 0)
+      else collapse()
+    }
+    const settleNow = (): void => {
+      const w = view.state.field(linkWriting)
+      if (w) settle(w, false)
+    }
+    return {
+      update(u: ViewUpdate) {
+        const was = u.startState.field(linkWriting)
+        const now = u.state.field(linkWriting)
+        if (was && now) {
+          const start = u.changes.mapPos(was.start, 1)
+          if (now.start !== start) settle({ start, was: was.was }, true)
+        }
+        if (now && u.selectionSet && !holds(now.start)) settle(now, true)
+      },
+      settleNow,
+      /** The host's way out: settles the link under edit and writes what `flush` memory queued. */
+      flush() {
+        settleNow()
+        for (const shown of queued.splice(0)) write(shown)
+      },
+    }
+  },
+  {
+    eventHandlers: {
+      // A blur settles alone: Chromium fires one as a focused editor is removed, and a cancelled field's queue must not write through it.
+      blur(e) {
+        if (!inCaretPane(e.relatedTarget)) this.settleNow()
+        return false
+      },
+    },
+  },
+)
```

```/Core/Properties/Pickers/ValueEditor.tsx diff
@@ -0 +1 @@
+import { useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useRef, type RefObject } from 'react'
+import { EditorView, keymap, placeholder } from '@codemirror/view'
+import { EditorState, Prec } from '@codemirror/state'
+import { history, historyKeymap, insertNewline } from '@codemirror/commands'
+import { invalidInput } from '@pommora/uix/Fields/fields.css'
+import { PICKER_PORTAL_ATTR } from '@pommora/uix/Pickers/PickerMenu'
+import { useLatest } from '@pommora/uix/Utilities/stableApi'
+import type { ConnPage } from '../../Connections/pageIndex'
+import { markdownLink } from '../../Connections/links'
+import { type EditorHost, heldPage, mirrorBody } from '../../MarkdownPM/api'
+import { editorBase } from '../../MarkdownPM/surface'
+import { focusRange } from '../../MarkdownPM/caretPlacement'
+import { drawnLinkAt } from '../../MarkdownPM/decorations'
+import { applyLinkAction } from '../../MarkdownPM/Links/linkEdit'
+import { linkSettle, type Remembers } from '../../MarkdownPM/Links/linkSettle'
+import { inCaretPane } from '../../MarkdownPM/Menus/caretPane'
+import { formatKeymap } from '../../MarkdownPM/Input/formatKeymap'
+import { useReconfigured } from '../../MarkdownPM/Input/useReconfigured'
+import { useConnectionAutocomplete } from '../../MarkdownPM/Autocomplete/useConnectionAutocomplete'
+import { AutocompletePane } from '../../MarkdownPM/Autocomplete/AutocompletePane'
+import './text-pane.css'
+
+const stopBubble = (e: { stopPropagation: () => void }): void => e.stopPropagation()
+
+const blanked = (doc: string): string => (doc.trim() === '' ? '' : doc)
+
+/** The one editor every property value is typed in: the Text pane's, and in `oneLine` mode a field's. Both save once on every way out; a field also ends its own edit, Return and blur committing unless the text is invalid, Escape cancelling, with the invalid state on the editor's own node. A commit settles the link under edit first, so what the leave would have written is what's read; a cancel ends the edit, so nothing after it, the unmount's save included, writes. */
+export function ValueEditor({
+  initial,
+  holder,
+  host,
+  oneLine = false,
+  remembers,
+  alias,
+  invalid,
+  saveRef,
+  onCommit,
+  onClose,
+}: {
+  initial: string
+  holder: ConnPage | undefined
+  host: EditorHost
+  oneLine?: boolean
+  remembers?: Remembers
+  /** Once mounted, seat the caret in the value's alias slot: the Link value's Rename. */
+  alias?: boolean
+  invalid?: (text: string) => boolean
+  saveRef?: RefObject<() => void>
+  onCommit: (text: string) => void
+  onClose: () => void
+}): React.JSX.Element {
+  const mountRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
+  const viewRef = useRef<EditorView | null>(null)
+  const committed = useRef(blanked(initial))
+  const ended = useRef(false)
+  const onCommitRef = useLatest(onCommit)
+  const onCloseRef = useLatest(onClose)
+  const invalidRef = useLatest(invalid)
+  const ac = useConnectionAutocomplete(viewRef, host, 'text')
+  const formatExt = useReconfigured(viewRef, host.settings().commands, formatKeymap)
+
+  const commit = (): void => {
+    const view = viewRef.current
+    if (!view || ended.current) return
+    view.plugin(linkSettle)?.flush()
+    const text = blanked(view.state.doc.toString())
+    if (text === committed.current) return
+    committed.current = text
+    onCommitRef.current(text)
+  }
+  const cancel = (): boolean => {
+    ended.current = true
+    onCloseRef.current()
+    return true
+  }
+  const leave = (): boolean => {
+    const view = viewRef.current
+    if (view && invalidRef.current?.(view.state.doc.toString())) return cancel()
+    commit()
+    onCloseRef.current()
+    return true
+  }
+  if (saveRef) saveRef.current = commit
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const view = new EditorView({
+      parent: mountRef.current!,
+      state: EditorState.create({
+        doc: initial,
+        extensions: [
+          editorBase({ host, scope: 'text', panes: [ac], formatExt, oneLine, remembers }),
+          heldPage.of(holder ?? null),
+          history(),
+          oneLine
+            ? [
+                EditorView.editorAttributes.of({ class: invalidInput }),
+                // A field holds one line: a typed or pasted break lands as a space.
+                EditorState.transactionFilter.of((tr) => {
+                  if (!tr.docChanged || tr.newDoc.lines === 1) return tr
+                  const breaks = []
+                  for (let i = 1; i < tr.newDoc.lines; i++) {
+                    const { to } = tr.newDoc.line(i)
+                    breaks.push({ from: to, to: to + 1, insert: ' ' })
+                  }
+                  return [tr, { changes: breaks, sequential: true }]
+                }),
+                EditorView.updateListener.of((u) => {
+                  if (u.docChanged && invalidRef.current)
+                    u.view.dom.setAttribute(
+                      'aria-invalid',
+                      String(invalidRef.current(u.state.doc.toString())),
+                    )
+                }),
+                EditorView.domEventHandlers({
+                  blur: (e) => {
+                    if (!inCaretPane(e.relatedTarget)) leave()
+                    return false
+                  },
+                }),
+              ]
+            : placeholder('Begin typing.'),
+          Prec.highest(
+            keymap.of([
+              { key: 'Enter', run: leave },
+              { key: 'Shift-Enter', run: oneLine ? () => true : insertNewline },
+              ...(oneLine
+                ? [
+                    { key: 'Mod-Enter', run: () => true },
+                    { key: 'Escape', run: cancel },
+                  ]
+                : [
+                    // A field lets Tab move the focus as a plain field does; the pane keeps it, and Shift-Tab stops short of its focus trap, which would carry it to the ×.
+                    { key: 'Tab', run: () => true },
+                    { key: 'Shift-Tab', run: () => true, stopPropagation: true },
+                  ]),
+            ]),
+          ),
+          keymap.of(historyKeymap),
+        ],
+      }),
+    })
+    viewRef.current = view
+    if (invalid) view.dom.setAttribute('aria-invalid', String(invalid(initial)))
+    const doc = view.state.doc.toString()
+    if (alias && drawnLinkAt(view, 0)) applyLinkAction(view, 'rename', [0, doc.length])
+    else if (alias) {
+      // A bare address draws no link token, so Rename gives it the label a markdown link has.
+      view.dispatch({ changes: { from: 0, to: doc.length, insert: markdownLink(doc, '') } })
+      focusRange(view, 1)
+    } else {
+      view.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: doc.length }, scrollIntoView: true })
+      view.focus()
+    }
+    // A popover blooms in from a scale the caret was measured through, so the editor measures again once it settles.
+    const portal = mountRef.current!.closest(`[${PICKER_PORTAL_ATTR}]`)
+    const remeasure = (): void => view.requestMeasure()
+    portal?.addEventListener('animationend', remeasure)
+    return () => {
+      portal?.removeEventListener('animationend', remeasure)
+      view.destroy()
+      viewRef.current = null
+    }
+  }, [])
+  // Saved in the mutation phase: a seat unmounting with the pane retires its writer in its own passive cleanup first, so a passive save here would be dropped.
+  useLayoutEffect(() => commit, [])
+  // An outside write lands only in an editor that holds nothing unsaved; the editor's own close then writes last, as a page body's merge does.
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const view = viewRef.current
+    if (
+      view &&
+      blanked(view.state.doc.toString()) === committed.current &&
+      initial !== committed.current
+    ) {
+      committed.current = initial
+      mirrorBody(view, initial)
+    }
+  }, [initial])
+
+  return (
+    <>
+      {/* The layer above cancels every right-click and a seat's click opens the edit; the editor's own menu and caret ask first, so both events stop here. */}
+      {/* biome-ignore lint/a11y/noStaticElementInteractions lint/a11y/useKeyWithClickEvents: a bubble guard, not a control */}
+      <div
+        className={oneLine ? 'value-field mdpm-shell' : 'text-pane-body mdpm-shell'}
+        onClick={stopBubble}
+        onContextMenu={stopBubble}
+      >
+        <div ref={mountRef} className="mdpm-editor" />
+      </div>
+      <AutocompletePane {...ac.pane} />
+    </>
+  )
+}
```

##### UIX/Pickers/FieldPicker.tsx

```/UIX/Pickers/FieldPicker.tsx diff
@@ -0 +1 @@
+import type { ReactNode, RefObject } from 'react'
+import { EditableInput } from '../Fields/EditableInput'
+import { PickerMenu } from './PickerMenu'
+import * as s from './field-picker.css'
+
+/** What the one chrome holds: the kit's input over a `value`, with its affixes, or a caller's own editor as `children`. */
+type Typed = {
+  value: string
+  onCommit: (next: string) => void
+  invalid?: (text: string) => boolean
+  leading?: ReactNode
+  trailing?: ReactNode
+  children?: undefined
+}
+type Hosted = {
+  children: ReactNode
+  value?: undefined
+  onCommit?: undefined
+  invalid?: undefined
+  leading?: undefined
+  trailing?: undefined
+}
+
+/** A typed value's popover: one field wrapper owning the fill, stroke, focus ring, type, and width, around either the kit's input or an editor the caller mounts. */
+export function FieldPicker({
+  open,
+  onDismiss,
+  triggerRef,
+  ...inner
+}: {
+  open: boolean
+  onDismiss: () => void
+  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
+} & (Typed | Hosted)): React.JSX.Element | null {
+  return (
+    <PickerMenu
+      open={open}
+      onDismiss={onDismiss}
+      triggerRef={triggerRef}
+      direction="down"
+      origin="center"
+      contentClassName={s.content}
+    >
+      <div className={s.field}>
+        {inner.value === undefined ? (
+          inner.children
+        ) : (
+          <>
+            {inner.leading !== undefined && <span className={s.leading}>{inner.leading}</span>}
+            <EditableInput
+              initial={inner.value}
+              className={s.suffixInput}
+              caretAtEnd
+              invalid={inner.invalid}
+              onCommit={inner.onCommit}
+              onCancel={onDismiss}
+            />
+            {inner.trailing !== undefined && <span className={s.trailing}>{inner.trailing}</span>}
+          </>
+        )}
+      </div>
+    </PickerMenu>
+  )
+}
```

##### UIX/Pickers/field-picker.css.ts

```/UIX/Pickers/field-picker.css.ts diff
@@ -0 +1 @@
+import { style } from '@vanilla-extract/css'
+import { vars } from '../Theme/color.css'
+import { font } from '../Theme/typography.css'
+import { base, field as kitField } from '../Fields/fields.css'
+import { focusRing } from '../Fields/fieldRing'
+
+const c = vars.color
+
+/** Left-anchored so the caret sits at the field's left edge, never centered. */
+export const content = style({ alignItems: 'flex-start' })
+
+/** The one chrome a typed value's popover wears: the fill, stroke, and focus ring, the control-size type, and a width that follows the content between its bounds; whatever sits inside owns no chrome of its own. */
+export const field = style([
+  kitField,
+  {
+    gap: '6px',
+    width: 'auto',
+    minWidth: '100px', // KNOB
+    maxWidth: '200px', // KNOB
+    overflow: 'hidden',
+    lineHeight: font.scale.control.line,
+    fontSize: font.scale.control.size,
+    fontWeight: font.weight.emphasized,
+    ...focusRing('within'),
+  },
+])
+
+/** No chrome — the wrapper owns the fill + stroke; sized to its text, scrolling past the wrapper's bound. */
+export const suffixInput = style([
+  base,
+  {
+    fieldSizing: 'content',
+    flex: '1 1 auto',
+    minWidth: 0,
+    minHeight: 0,
+    whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
+    overflowX: 'auto',
+    overflowY: 'hidden',
+    scrollbarWidth: 'none',
+    vars: { '--scroll-fade': 'var(--fade-light)' },
+  },
+])
+
+export const leading = style({
+  flex: '0 0 auto',
+  display: 'inline-flex',
+  color: c.label.secondary,
+  fontWeight: font.weight.semibold,
+})
+
+/** The "/ N" out-of hint — pinned, never scrolling. */
+export const trailing = style({
+  flex: '0 0 auto',
+  whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
+  color: c.label.tertiary,
+})
```

````/Core/MarkdownPM/Links/linkSettle.test.ts diff
+    for (const [initialBody, typed] of [
+      ['a [[Alpha|]] b', ''],
+      ['a [[Alpha|]] b', 'on'],
+    ] as const) {
+      const view = await mountEditor({
+        initialBody,
+        connections: conn,
+        host: { aliases: { p1: ['one'] } },
+      })
+      vi.spyOn(view, 'coordsAtPos').mockReturnValue({ left: 10, right: 10, top: 10, bottom: 20 })
+      const edit = vi.spyOn(harnessState().host.aliases, 'edit')
+      await act(async () => view.focus())
+      await caretTo(view, 10)
+      if (typed)
+        await act(async () => {
+          view.dispatch({
+            changes: { from: 10, insert: typed },
+            selection: { anchor: 10 + typed.length },
+            userEvent: 'input.type',
+          })
+        })
+      const pane = document.querySelector('.mdpm-ac') as HTMLElement
+      await act(async () => {
+        view.contentDOM.dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('blur', { relatedTarget: pane }))
+      })
+      expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe(`a [[Alpha|${typed}]] b`)
+      expect(edit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+      await cleanupEditor()
+    }
+  })
+})
+
+describe('an emptied markdown label shows its target, as an emptied alias drops its pipe', () => {
+  it.each([
+    ['a [x](Alpha) b', 'a [Alpha](Alpha) b'],
+    ['a [x](Alpha#Intro) b', 'a [Intro](Alpha#Intro) b'],
+    ['a [x](https://example.com) b', 'a [](https://example.com) b'],
+    ['a ![x](Alpha) b', 'a ![Alpha](Alpha) b'],
+  ])('emptying and leaving %s gives %s', async (initialBody, written) => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody, connections: conn })
+    const at = initialBody.indexOf('x') + 1
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, at)
+    await emptyBefore(view, at)
+    await caretTo(view, 0)
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe(written)
+  })
+
+  it('keeps a rest at the link’s end, mapped past the label it fills', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: 'a [x](Alpha) b', connections: conn })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, 4)
+    await emptyBefore(view, 4)
+    const end = 'a [](Alpha)'.length
+    await act(async () => {
+      view.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: end }, effects: restedOnLink.of(end) })
+      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0))
+    })
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('a [Alpha](Alpha) b')
+    expect(view.state.field(linkRest)).toBe('a [Alpha](Alpha)'.length)
+  })
+
+  it('fills on blur without waiting for a timer', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: 'a [x](Alpha) b', connections: conn })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, 4)
+    await emptyBefore(view, 4)
+    view.contentDOM.dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('blur'))
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('a [Alpha](Alpha) b')
+  })
+
+  it('waits for the caret to leave the whole link, the gap between label and target included', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: 'a [x](Alpha) b', connections: conn })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, 4)
+    await emptyBefore(view, 4)
+    for (const at of [4, 5]) await caretTo(view, at)
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('a [](Alpha) b')
+    await caretTo(view, 0)
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('a [Alpha](Alpha) b')
+  })
+
+  it('an empty label the caret only passes through, or arrows across, stays as written', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: 'a [](Alpha) b', connections: conn })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    for (const at of [3, 4, 5, 0]) await caretTo(view, at)
+    view.contentDOM.dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('blur'))
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('a [](Alpha) b')
+  })
+
+  it('a label typed empty with its page typed out in full is filled once the caret leaves', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: '', connections: conn })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await typeInto(view, '[](Alpha')
+    await caretTo(view, view.state.doc.length)
+    await caretTo(view, 0)
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('[Alpha](Alpha)')
+  })
+})
+
+describe('an alias left in raw HTML stays as written', () => {
+  it('keeps an emptied slot’s pipe when the caret leaves it', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({
+      initialBody: '<div>\na [[Alpha|x]] b\n</div>',
+      connections: conn,
+      host: { settings: { htmlFormatting: true } },
+    })
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, 17)
+    await emptyBefore(view, 17)
+    await caretTo(view, 0)
+    expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe('<div>\na [[Alpha|]] b\n</div>')
+  })
+})
+
+describe('an alias left in code stays as written', () => {
+  it('keeps an emptied slot’s pipe or hash', async () => {
+    for (const [initialBody, anchor, emptiedBody] of [
+      ['```\na [[Alpha|x]] b\n```', 15, '```\na [[Alpha|]] b\n```'],
+      ['a `[[Alpha#x]]` b', 12, 'a `[[Alpha#]]` b'],
+    ] as const) {
+      const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody, connections: conn })
+      await act(async () => view.focus())
+      await caretTo(view, anchor)
+      await emptyBefore(view, anchor)
+      await caretTo(view, 0)
+      expect(view.state.doc.toString()).toBe(emptiedBody)
+      await cleanupEditor()
+    }
+  })
+
+  it('remembers no alias typed there', async () => {
+    const view = await mountEditor({ initialBody: '```\na [[Alpha|]] b\n```', connections: conn })
+    const edit = vi.spyOn(harnessState().host.aliases, 'edit')
+    await act(async () => view.focus())
+    await caretTo(view, 14)
+    await act(async () => {
+      view.dispatch({
+        changes: { from: 14, insert: 'new' },
+        selection: { anchor: 17 },
+        userEvent: 'input.type',
+      })
+    })
+    await caretTo(view, 0)
+    expect(edit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+})
````

```/Core/Properties/Pickers/ValueEditor.test.tsx diff
+// @vitest-environment jsdom

+stubEditorBridge()
+
+const conn: ConnectionsApi = {

+  headingsOf: () => undefined,
+  open: () => {},
+}
+const host = { ...testHost(), connections: () => conn }
+const onCommit = vi.fn()
+const onClose = vi.fn()
+let container: HTMLDivElement
+let root: Root
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  onCommit.mockClear()
+  onClose.mockClear()
+  container = document.createElement('div')
+  document.body.appendChild(container)
+  root = createRoot(container)
+})
+afterEach(() => {
+  act(() => root.unmount())
+  container.remove()
+  for (const n of document.querySelectorAll('[data-picker-portal]')) n.remove()
+})
+
+const mount = (

+  props: Partial<Parameters<typeof ValueEditor>[0]> = {},
+): EditorView => {
+  act(() =>
+    root.render(
+      <ValueEditor

+        holder={undefined}
+        host={host}
+        oneLine
+        onCommit={onCommit}
+        onClose={onClose}
+        {...props}
+      />,
+    ),
+  )
+  const dom = container.querySelector('.cm-editor')
+  const view = dom && EditorView.findFromDOM(dom as HTMLElement)
+  if (!view) throw new Error('no editor')
+  return view
+}
+const doc = (view: EditorView): string => view.state.doc.toString()
+const press = (view: EditorView, key: string, mods: Partial<KeyboardEventInit> = {}): boolean => {
+  const e = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...mods })
+  act(() => {
+    view.contentDOM.dispatchEvent(e)
+  })
+  return e.defaultPrevented
+}
+const type = (view: EditorView, insert: string, userEvent = 'input.type'): void =>
+  act(() => {
+    const { from, to } = view.state.selection.main
+    view.dispatch({
+      changes: { from, to, insert },
+      selection: { anchor: from + insert.length },
+      userEvent,
+    })
+  })
+const blur = (view: EditorView, relatedTarget: Element | null = null): void =>
+  act(() => {
+    view.contentDOM.dispatchEvent(new FocusEvent('blur', { relatedTarget }))
+  })
+

+    expect(onCommit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })

+    type(view, '', 'delete.backward')

+    press(view, 'Enter')
+    press(view, 'Enter')
+    expect(onCommit).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('[[Alpha]]')
+  })
+})
+
+describe('ValueEditor and alias memory', () => {
+  const remembered = (remembers?: Remembers): ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn> => {
+    const edit = vi.spyOn(host.aliases, 'edit')
+    const view = mount('[[Alpha|]]', { remembers })
+    act(() => view.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: 8 } }))
+    type(view, 'nick')
+    press(view, 'Enter')
+    press(view, 'Enter')
+    expect(onCommit).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('[[Alpha|nick]]')
+    return edit
+  }
+  afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())
+
+  it('remembers a typed alias on leave by default', () => {
+    expect(remembered()).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('p1', { op: 'add', alias: 'nick' })
+  })
+
+  it('remembers nothing where the caller holds the memory', () => {
+    expect(remembered('never')).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+
+  // The alias typed, and the caret moved out of its link, which is where `leave` memory would write.
+  const left = (): { view: EditorView; edit: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn> } => {
+    const edit = vi.spyOn(host.aliases, 'edit')
+    const view = mount('[[Alpha|]]', { remembers: 'flush' })
+    act(() => view.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: 8 } }))
+    type(view, 'nick')
+    act(() => view.dispatch({ selection: { anchor: doc(view).length } }))
+    expect(edit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    return { view, edit }
+  }
+
+  it('under flush, remembers once the edit commits', () => {
+    const { view, edit } = left()
+    press(view, 'Enter')
+    expect(onCommit).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('[[Alpha|nick]]')
+    expect(edit).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('p1', { op: 'add', alias: 'nick' })
+  })
+
+  it('under flush, Escape remembers nothing, through the blur a removed editor fires included', () => {
+    const { view, edit } = left()
+    press(view, 'Escape')
+    blur(view)
+    act(() => root.unmount())
+    root = createRoot(container)
+    expect(onCommit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+    expect(edit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()
+  })
+})
```

```/.claude/HistoryPM.md diff
+#### PM-152 || Text Colors & Highlighting
+**DATE:** 10-15-2026
+
+Highlight colors, introduced in PM-113 with an emoji on both sides of the words, came to be written with one leading emoji (`==🔴words==`), and the machinery that kept the two in step was removed. A text color (`=🔴words=`) joined highlights as a second paint over the same color registry, in seven colors, offered from a Text Color submenu above Highlight and through the shared Change Color menu; a span takes one color, and picking the other paint converts it. Either paint holds connections, links, code, and math, closing only on a marker outside them, and a link inside a text color takes its color, underlined. The right-click menu came to read a selection the same way a pick writes it, a paint is written only where it reads back as that paint, and the highlight chord removes either paint it lands in while the Accent row recolors. Sapphire extended Obsidian's own highlights to every Pommora color and shape and painted text color in both of its views.
+
```

##### .claude/IssuesPM.md

```/.claude/IssuesPM.md diff
@@ -1 +1 @@
-## Pommora Codebase Audit
-
-**Pinned:** `f6511401d` (09-23-2026) · **Reconciled:** `5272eb82f` (10-15-2026) · **Findings:** 87/643
-
-Thirty-four Opus investigators read every production file in `Core`, `UIX`, `Desktop`, and `Sync` in full, sliced by folder and by the jobs the code performs. Two mergers combined their 857 candidates by root cause, and twenty-one reviewers who hadn't raised them re-read every citation, reproduced the High ones against real modules, and killed 63. This document is the current state: findings that were fixed, withdrawn, or ruled moot are removed rather than annotated, and rulings are written into the findings they settle. The readiness and pace sections are the orchestrator's judgment, drawn from the evidence below them. A system audit of MarkdownPM (10-08-2026) read the editor in full at `70fc6063c`, and a workstream audit of Connections and Aliases (10-15-2026) read that surface at `5272eb82f`; the findings of both are folded in here.
-
-### Verdict
-
-#### Readiness
-
-**Plumb first, narrowly.** Four findings are High. Three are in Sync: F-001 and F-003 were reproduced against the real code, and F-007 was traced through it by two readers. Each is in code that saves, syncs, or deletes a person's files. The fourth is in the page editor: F-044 freezes typing on very long pages. The surrounding structure is sound, and the fixes are contained.
-
-**What holds, with evidence:**
-
-- **The layering rules all pass their checks.**
-  - Core reaches the machine only through `Core/Platform`: zero Node or Electron imports across 700 Core and UIX files.
-  - The code the host runs imports no React: 205 files, verified by `engineGraph.test.ts` and `hostGraph.test.ts`.
-  - UIX imports nothing from Core.
-  - Every channel is declared once in `bridge.ts`, and one `catch` turns a thrown error into a `Result`.
-- **The pure models hold.** The view pipeline and the tile layout model produced no High findings, and their Medium findings are about cost and duplication, not wrong results. The connections layer produced no High findings either, though W22 finds most of its rules stated twice and a few small wrong results where the copies disagree.
-
-**What's broken, and where:**
-
-| Area | State | High | Medium |
-| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
-| Sync | Changes from another device are written to whatever path the hub names, including outside the Nexus and into `.git/` or `.obsidian/` (F-001). A rebuilt or restored hub never gets unchanged files re-uploaded, so new devices receive a partial Nexus (F-003). A list two devices both edited keeps one device's items, so a Context rename can revert and hide its Spaces (F-006). Trashing a Collection or Set uploads the contents of its excluded folders (F-007). | 3 | 4 |
-| Page editor | Past about 8,000 lines, the footer's figures re-tokenize the whole page on every typing pause, freezing the editor for up to a second (F-044). | 1 | 8 |
-| Menus and pickers | The kit's buttons show no keyboard focus, so a Tab walk through a menu or toolbar loses its place on every button (F-076). | 0 | 1 |
-| Identity | An ID lost or damaged outside the app is replaced rather than recovered on every path but a held page's own event, so tabs, pins, metadata, and a Nexus's device store lose what they were keyed to (F-089). | 0 | 1 |
-| Connections | A link is read by two markdown grammars, resolved by two readers, and edited through two trackers in one listener, so a heading renamed into something a wikilink can't spell strands its wikilinks (F-122), a heading picked into an aliased wikilink rests the caret inside the alias (F-120), and a lone `![Alias](Page)` line draws a graph edge (F-127). | 0 | 6 |
-
-**What extending costs today:**
-
-| Addition | Files Touched | Ways to Do a Step | Grade |
-| ------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
-| A new entity kind | ~20 | 1 | Moderate: every kind list reads `entities.ts`, and the compiler names each switch and table the new kind must fill |
-| A new property type | 4 plus its editor | 1 | Cheap: one record entry, and the compiler names each table that still needs the type |
-| A new editor construct | ~12 inline · ~18 block | 4 | Moderate: block rules are read from one place, and the word counter reads inline constructs from the tokenizer |
-| A new view renderer | 3–4 plus the renderer | 4 | Moderate |
-| A new link syntax or link surface | ~12 | 3 | Costly: two markdown grammars, two target readers, and the picker's seven form names each take it by hand; after W22, one grammar and one picker axis |
-| A new floating window | 3–5 | 1 | Cheap |
-| A new persisted setting | 2–3 synced · 2 per device | 4 | Cheap |
-| A new host channel | 2–5 | 5 | Cheap |
-
-#### Pace Guidance
-
-**Too fast for verification, not too fast for design.** Pommora has taken 3,955 commits since 05-10-2026, 1,896 of them in the last sixty days. The design choices hold up under that speed. The checking behind each change doesn't.

-### Workstreams
-
-#### W1 · Sync Paths, Renames, and Resync
-
-These are the ways a change travelling between devices can land in the wrong place, at two names, or not at all: an unchecked path from the hub, renames racing edits, capitalization that differs between devices, and a hub that was rebuilt or restored. Landing them makes the wire path-safe and a rebuilt hub whole again. It sits in the first tier because sync spreads any one device's mistake to every device.
-
-##### F-001 · Changes from other devices are written to whatever path the hub names, including outside the Nexus.
-
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Integrity · **Weight:** High · **Size:** S · **Net:** +12 · **Origin:** Drift
-
-**Finding**
+### A1 • Sync & Devices
 
-When another device's change arrives, the app writes, deletes, or moves the file at the path the hub's log names, with no check that the path stays inside the Nexus or inside the set of files sync may touch. A path like `../x` lands outside the Nexus folder, and a change into `.git/`, `.obsidian/`, or an excluded folder lands even though sync rules keep those at home; the hub rejects `..` but not `\`, so on Windows a peer's `a\..\..\x` becomes traversal. A compromised hub, or any editor device through the hub, can place any blob it holds at any path, and by naming an outside file in a delete it can make the app upload that file first, encrypted with the Nexus key every device holds. The documented promise that binding each blob to its path keeps the hub from moving ciphertext between paths holds only for decryption, since the landing path is never compared with it, and with NexusOS also an Obsidian vault, a planted `.obsidian/` plugin or `.git/config` is code that later runs on the receiving machine. Pull tests with hand-built changes landed a write for `../escaped.md` outside the Nexus root, a real page's write replayed as `../planted.md` (which still decrypts), and a write into `.git/hooks/post-commit`, because only reconcile gates arrivals through `manifestAdmits` while the live pull and `resolveStale` don't.[^1]
-
-**Fix | Proposed**
-
-Add one arrival gate in `Core/Sync/Arrival`: a change lands only if `manifestAdmits(session.scope)` accepts `change.path` (and `change.from` for a rename), the path carries no `\`, and a `write` change's `path` equals its `record.path`; otherwise it's skipped, the cursor advances, and status names it. Call it at the top of `landChange` and `resolveStale`; `manifestAdmits` already rejects a leading `..` or `/`, every dot segment but a top-level `.nexus`, every `_`-prefixed folder, and every excluded folder, so it's the survivor. Add `\` to the hub's `itemPath` refusal.
-
-##### F-002 · A misbehaving sync hub can crash the app by sending an enormous reply.
+#### F-007 • Trashing a Collection or Set uploads the contents of its excluded folders to Sync.
 
-> **Area:** Desktop · **Lens:** Integrity · **Weight:** Low · **Size:** S · **Net:** +5 · **Origin:** Shortcut
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| High | Medium (=🟢+15=) | Drift | `93baa6931` | **Created:** 10-01-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
-A sync hub, hostile or broken, can crash the whole app by sending back a reply that never ends. The hub limits the size of every request it accepts, but the app buffers whatever the hub sends back into memory before looking at it, and the transport runs in the Electron main process. An unbounded reply takes the app down, and the session restarts on every launch. `transport.ts:26` collects chunks with `res.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk))` and keeps no running total, and `call.ts:90` casts `JSON.parse(reply.body)` to the route's reply type with no shape check.[^2]
+Sync admits nothing under an excluded folder, so its files stay on the device. When a Collection or Set holding an excluded folder is deleted to the Nexus Trash, the whole folder moves into its bundle, and Sync uploads the excluded folder's files from there, encrypted, to the hub and on to every device. `deleteOp` moves the folder into its bundle through `relocate`, which reports the rename to Sync's write tap; `feedRename` hands it to `pushRename`, whose trailing `pushDirty([to])` lists the bundle folder through `manifestAdmits`. Its `.trash` arm matches the path past `.trash/` against the excluded list, which `releaseExcludedFolders` empties of the deleted folder's entries as the delete finishes, and which a bundle's path can't match in any case, since the stamped `<stamp>__<Name>.deleted` folder sits between the parent folders and the entity's name. `pushDirty` keeps a Markdown file home only when it carries no `ID:`, so within Sync's usual size and name limits the upload takes the non-Markdown files and the pages carrying an ID, which includes the pages of a folder excluded after they were stamped.[^7]
 
-**Fix | Proposed**
+**Solution** [TBD]
 
-Add `TransportRequest.maxBytes`, set by `call` (a fixed JSON reply cap, such as 4 MiB) and by `getBlob` (`BLOB_CAP` plus `SEAL_OVERHEAD`); the transport keeps a running total and destroys the request past it. Checking the paths a reply names belongs to F-001.
+A bundle's record already keeps the excluded entries the Collection or Set held (`excluded`), which a restore reseats. Sync's admission of a Trash path reads those kept entries, so a file under a bundle's excluded entry stays home in the Trash as it did in place. Where the kept entries live for a synchronous admit, whether folded into the scope at arm time and by each delete and empty or read from each bundle's record, is this fix's design.
 
-##### F-003 · Reconnecting to a rebuilt or restored hub never re-uploads unchanged files.
+#### F-003 • Reconnecting to a rebuilt or restored hub never re-uploads unchanged files.
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Defect · **Weight:** High · **Size:** M · **Net:** +10 · **Origin:** Patch-Over
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| High | Medium (=🟢+10=) | Patch-Over | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
 Each device keeps a record of what it believes the hub already holds, and when the hub loses its history (its data folder wiped and re-created at the same address, or restored from an older backup), the device keeps trusting that record and never re-uploads unchanged files. Reconcile sees files the hub has never heard of and hands them to the ordinary push, which skips every one whose bytes still match the stale record, so only files edited afterward reach the new hub and a device joining later gets a partial Nexus with nobody told. This breaks the documented recovery path, "the hub copy is rebuilt from one device" (Decision Log B′-4), whenever the rebuilt hub keeps its address. A second device rejoining after the rebuilt hub's change counter has passed its old cursor gets no `resync` answer at all, so it never reconciles, never re-uploads its unchanged files, and misses the rebuilt hub's changes numbered at or below its old cursor. Against the fake hub that mirrors `Sync/Store/log.ts`, two files were reconciled, the hub state wiped, and `reconcile` run again, which sent zero `/store` requests and left zero hub items.[^3]
 
-**Fix | TBD**
+**Solution** [TBD]
 
 Two moves, closing different gaps. In `reconcile`, drop a base row whose path has no head in the heads read before the push (`if (head === undefined) deleteBase(rel)` ahead of `toPush.push(rel)`), so the push sends it as a new write; this fixes the first device back after a wipe or a restore. Then tie the binding to the hub's history rather than its address: the key record's KDF salt is minted only when the hub's record is created (`freshKdfParams`), so `SyncScope` stores `salt` at bind, `sync:connect` treats the binding as kept only when address and salt both match, and `withKeys` compares `info.kdf.salt` with the binding before `begin` and, on a mismatch, drops every base row and resets the cursor to 0 so `begin` runs the first-bind reconcile; this fixes every later device after a wipe. A hub restored from backup keeps its salt, so a device whose old cursor it has already re-passed stays undetected until the hub issues a history epoch, and a future password change under fresh KDF parameters would trigger one harmless full reconcile.
 
-##### F-004 · Renaming a page while another device's edit is in flight leaves the page at both names.
-
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Defect · **Weight:** Medium · **Size:** S · **Net:** +10 · **Origin:** Drift
-
-**Finding**
-
-Renaming a page while another device's edit to it hasn't reached this device yet leaves the same page ID at two paths, which the duplicate-ID judge then splits into two pages. The hub refuses the rename and answers with the other device's edit at the old name, but the app moves its record to the new name anyway and settles the conflict as if that edit belonged there, so the rename is never re-sent. If this device's copy wins, the hub holds the page at both names; if the other device's copy wins, it lands at the old name and the renamed file stays behind unsynced. A local-wins stale rename left the hub with live items `['Notes/One.md', 'Notes/Renamed.md']`, because `pushRename` calls `renameBase` for every outcome (`push.ts:239`) and passes the destination to `resolveStale` with the head read at the source (`push.ts:241`).[^4]
-
-**Fix | Proposed**
-
-On a stale rename, keep the base row at `from`: fetch the head's bytes, pick the winner against the bytes now at `to` with `newerSide` (capturing the loser as `resolveStale` does), land the winner at `to`, record the base at `from` under `head.seq`, and re-send the rename with that base. `renameBase` moves only on an accepted outcome.
-
-##### F-005 · Renaming a Set on one device leaves an empty ghost Set on the others.
+#### F-001 • Changes from other devices are written to whatever path the hub names, including outside the Nexus.
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Defect · **Weight:** Medium · **Size:** S · **Net:** +5 · **Origin:** Drift
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| High | Small (=🟢+12=) | Drift | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
-Renaming a Set on one device leaves an empty folder under the old name on every other device, which Pommora reads as an empty Set. Folders don't travel through sync, only files: a Set rename sends one rename per file inside it, so each receiving device moves the files and leaves the old folder behind. Deleting nested Sets leaves the outer folder behind the same way, because a delete prunes only its immediate parent, and that prune uses a recursive remove that would take any file created there between the check and the remove. Landing `Notes/Ideas/One.md` and `_pageset.json` renamed to `Notes/Plans/` left `Notes` holding both an empty `Ideas` and `Plans`, since `landRename` has no parent cleanup and `resolveFolderKind` returns `'set'` for any nested folder.[^5]
+When another device's change arrives, the app writes, deletes, or moves the file at the path the hub's log names, with no check that the path stays inside the Nexus or inside the set of files sync may touch. A path like `../x` lands outside the Nexus folder, and a change into `.git/`, `.obsidian/`, or an excluded folder lands even though sync rules keep those at home; the hub rejects `..` but not `\`, so on Windows a peer's `a\..\..\x` becomes traversal. A compromised hub, or any editor device through the hub, can place any blob it holds at any path, and by naming an outside file in a delete it can make the app upload that file first, encrypted with the Nexus key every device holds. The documented promise that binding each blob to its path keeps the hub from moving ciphertext between paths holds only for decryption, since the landing path is never compared with it, and with NexusOS also an Obsidian vault, a planted `.obsidian/` plugin or `.git/config` is code that later runs on the receiving machine. Pull tests with hand-built changes landed a write for `../escaped.md` outside the Nexus root, a real page's write replayed as `../planted.md` (which still decrypts), and a write into `.git/hooks/post-commit`, because only reconcile gates arrivals through `manifestAdmits` while the live pull and `resolveStale` don't.[^1]
 
-**Fix | Proposed**
+**Solution** [Proposed]
 
-Add one `pruneEmptyParents(root, rel)` in `land.ts` that walks up from the vacated path's parent to the first non-empty folder or the root, re-reading each folder immediately before removing it, used by both `landDelete` and `landRename`.
+Add one arrival gate in `Core/Sync/Arrival`: a change lands only if `manifestAdmits(session.scope)` accepts `change.path` (and `change.from` for a rename), the path carries no `\`, and a `write` change's `path` equals its `record.path`; otherwise it's skipped, the cursor advances, and status names it. Call it at the top of `landChange` and `resolveStale`; `manifestAdmits` already rejects a leading `..` or `/`, every dot segment but a top-level `.nexus`, every `_`-prefixed folder, and every excluded folder, so it's the survivor. Add `\` to the hub's `itemPath` refusal.
 
-##### F-006 · Two devices editing different items in one synced list keep only one device's edits, and a lost Context rename hides that Context's Spaces.
+#### F-006 • Two devices editing different items in one synced list keep only one device's edits, and a lost Context rename hides that Context's Spaces.
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Integrity · **Weight:** Medium · **Size:** M · **Net:** +40 · **Origin:** Shortcut
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| Moderate | Medium (=🟢+40=) | Shortcut | `0c80012cb` | **Created:** 09-26-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-16-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
 When a synced Pommora JSON file has changed on both devices, arrival merges it key by key against the last synced copy. A key that only one side changed takes that side's value. A key that both sides changed goes whole to the newer side, and the merge descends only into objects that `mergeDepthFor` names. A list never descends, because the gate admits only plain objects and `isPlainObject` rejects arrays. So a list of items with ids merges as one value, and the losing side's items are dropped. The Sync feature doc records this as design ("a merged JSON file keeps its losing keys nowhere"), which leaves item-level merging as the only protection.
 
@@ -140 +206 @@ Some lists are out of scope:
 
 Sync runs between desktops today. Two online devices converge within seconds through the long poll and a 2.5 s debounce, so the ordinary window is a device that edits while offline. A Mobile companion widens that window. In a probe of the real modules, a registry rename against an add kept `Projects` and `People` and lost `Work`. A tile add against a restyle kept `bands:[1,2]` with only `t1` in `tiles`. A sidecar's views and properties kept only the remote side, and select options kept `c` and lost `b`.[^6]
 
-**Fix | Proposed**
+**Solution** [Proposed]
 
 Teach `mergeKeys` one structural case. At a level above 0, when base, local and remote are all arrays whose every element is a plain object with a unique string `id`, merge item by item at `level − 1`:
 
@@ -156 +222 @@ Any other array stays whole. Set a sidecar's `properties` to merge as a set. `me
 
 Option lists key on `value`, which a rename changes, so they stay whole. Add one sentence to `NexusSyncPM.md`'s merge paragraph. Per-item merging refines the Concurrency decision's per-section updates the same way the per-definition and per-field merges already do. **Your call:** approval under that Locked Decision.

-#### W2 · Sync Keys and Device Membership
-
-Revoking a device, rotating the encryption key, and renaming or removing devices each leave a gap between what the settings promise and what the devices do. F-008 carries the one decision about what revocation guarantees, and F-009 is only worth landing under one answer to it. They sit together because they share the key ring and its rotation.
+#### F-004 • Renaming a page while another device's edit is in flight leaves the page at both names.
 
-##### F-008 · A revoked device that knows the Nexus password can still unlock the new key.
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| Moderate | Small (=🟢+10=) | Drift | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Integrity · **Weight:** Low · **Size:** S · **Net:** 0 · **Origin:** Shortcut
+**Description**
 
-**Finding**
-
-A revoke mints a new content key and wraps it for each remaining device and for the Nexus password, but the password doesn't change, so a revoked device that holds it can unwrap the new key from the hub's key record. Every device that created or joined the Nexus by typing the password keeps it in its keychain. What actually keeps a revoked device out of content stored afterward is the hub refusing its requests, not cryptography, so the documented promise that "a revoked device can read nothing stored after its revocation" (Decision Log D-4, NexusSyncPM §The Keys) is false for any revoked device that holds the password. `rotateRing` derives its key-encryption key from the stored password and appends `wrapForPassword([raw], kek)` (`handlers.ts:177,193`), and `openWithPassword` unwraps every `holder === 'password'` entry (`keyring.ts:40-44`).[^8]
+Renaming a page while another device's edit to it hasn't reached this device yet leaves the same page ID at two paths, which the duplicate-ID judge then splits into two pages. The hub refuses the rename and answers with the other device's edit at the old name, but the app moves its record to the new name anyway and settles the conflict as if that edit belonged there, so the rename is never re-sent. If this device's copy wins, the hub holds the page at both names; if the other device's copy wins, it lands at the old name and the renamed file stays behind unsynced. A local-wins stale rename left the hub with live items `['Notes/One.md', 'Notes/Renamed.md']`, because `pushRename` calls `renameBase` for every outcome (`push.ts:239`) and passes the destination to `resolveStale` with the head read at the source (`push.ts:241`).[^4]
 
-**Fix | TBD**
+**Solution** [Proposed]
 
-Two moves are possible: restate the guarantee as hub-enforced for password holders (a doc edit in NexusSyncPM §The Keys and Decision Log D-4), or make a revoke also change the password, with `rotateRing` taking a new password and re-wrapping the whole ring under fresh KDF parameters (the re-wrap B′-1 already describes, though changing a password is deferred today because no channel carries the re-wrap); F-009 is only worth fixing under the second. **Your call:** restate the guarantee as hub-enforced for password holders (a doc edit), or make a revoke also change the password by re-wrapping the ring under fresh KDF parameters.
+On a stale rename, keep the base row at `from`: fetch the head's bytes, pick the winner against the bytes now at `to` with `newerSide` (capturing the loser as `resolveStale` does), land the winner at `to`, record the base at `from` under `head.seq`, and re-send the rename with that base. `renameBase` moves only on an accepted outcome.
 
-##### F-009 · After a revoke, other devices keep encrypting new content with the old key.
+#### F-005 • Renaming a Set on one device leaves an empty ghost Set on the others.
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Integrity · **Weight:** Low · **Size:** M · **Net:** +8 · **Origin:** Patch-Over
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| Moderate | Small (=🟢+5=) | Drift | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
-Revoking a device mints a fresh content key so the revoked device can't read anything stored afterward, but only the revoking device's running session switches to it. Every other running device keeps encrypting with the old key, which the revoked device holds, until it restarts or happens to decrypt something sealed under the new key. If the revoking device then goes idle, the others can keep writing under the compromised key indefinitely, so "every store after that uses the new key" (Decision Log D-4) doesn't hold. The hub still refuses the revoked device on every route, so the gap matters only when the hub leaks blobs. `act` sets `running.ring = rotated` for the local session only (`handlers.ts:240-243`), while other devices seal with `newest(session.ring)` (`push.ts:88`), which changes only in `openRecord`'s `unknown-key` catch and at session start.[^9]
+Renaming a Set on one device leaves an empty folder under the old name on every other device, which Pommora reads as an empty Set. Folders don't travel through sync, only files: a Set rename sends one rename per file inside it, so each receiving device moves the files and leaves the old folder behind. Deleting nested Sets leaves the outer folder behind the same way, because a delete prunes only its immediate parent, and that prune uses a recursive remove that would take any file created there between the check and the remove. Landing `Notes/Ideas/One.md` and `_pageset.json` renamed to `Notes/Plans/` left `Notes` holding both an empty `Ideas` and `Plans`, since `landRename` has no parent cleanup and `resolveFolderKind` returns `'set'` for any nested folder.[^5]
 
-**Fix | TBD**
+**Solution** [Proposed]
 
-The hub's `pull` reply carries the key record's `version` (it already bumps on every ring append); the session keeps the version its ring came from, and a pull answering a higher one reloads the ring (`reloaded`) before the next seal, so every running device switches within one 25-second poll. **Your call:** this is worth doing only if revocation stays cryptographic under the call in F-008.

-##### F-010 · A non-owner device's Revoke changes the encryption key, then fails, cutting the other device off.
+#### F-010 • A non-owner device's Revoke changes the encryption key, then fails, cutting the other device off.
 
-> **Area:** Sync · **Lens:** Defect · **Weight:** Medium · **Size:** S · **Net:** +4 · **Origin:** Drift
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| Moderate | Mini (=🟢+4=) | Drift | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Finding**
+**Description**
 
 Pressing Revoke on a device that isn't the Nexus owner changes the encryption key and then fails, leaving the target device approved but unable to read anything written afterward. Every approved device that holds the Nexus password sees a Revoke button on every other device; on a non-owner it first mints a new key and adds it to the hub's key ring for everyone except the target (any editor may), then asks the hub to revoke, which only the owner may do. The target never gets the new key, so once anything is written under it, every pull fails and the target stops receiving changes with no path to recover. `act` never checks this device's role before `rotateRing` appends under the editor-level `ring` route (`handlers.ts:230-237`), the owner-only `revoke` then fails with 404, and on the target `loadRing` returns only its device-wrapped entries, which lack the new key, so `decryptItem` throws `unknown-key` on every poll.[^10]
 
-**Fix | Literal**
+**Solution** [Literal]
 
 In `act('revoke')`, refuse before rotating unless this device's row in `devices` has `role === 'owner'`, and hide Revoke in `NexusRows` for non-owners from the same listing.
 
-##### F-011 · A device revoked while the app was closed thinks it's waiting for approval and never drops its keys.
+#### F-009 • After a revoke, other devices keep encrypting new content with the old key.

+**Description**
 
-A device revoked while the app was closed shows "Waiting for approval from another device", keeps its password and key ring in the keychain, and polls the hub every minute forever. Whether this device has been revoked is worked out in three places, three ways: a running session concludes "revoked", stops, and forgets its keys; the settings panel concludes "revoked" but only in its reply; and session start reads the same answer as "waiting for approval" and retries. A revoke deletes the membership row so every gated route answers 404 `not-found`, which `withKeys` treats as pending and retries (`session.ts:183-189`) while `pullWait` and `state` each test it with their own condition (`pull.ts:74-76`, `handlers.ts:124`).[^11]
+Revoking a device mints a fresh content key so the revoked device can't read anything stored afterward, but only the revoking device's running session switches to it. Every other running device keeps encrypting with the old key, which the revoked device holds, until it restarts or happens to decrypt something sealed under the new key. If the revoking device then goes idle, the others can keep writing under the compromised key indefinitely, so "every store after that uses the new key" (Decision Log D-4) doesn't hold. The hub still refuses the revoked device on every route, so the gap matters only when the hub leaks blobs. `act` sets `running.ring = rotated` for the local session only (`handlers.ts:240-243`), while other devices seal with `newest(session.ring)` (`push.ts:88`), which changes only in `openRecord`'s `unknown-key` catch and at session start.[^9]

-Add one `isRevoked(host, nexusId, outcome)` in `keyring.ts` (404 `not-found` with a cached device ring), used by `pullWait`, `state`, and `withKeys`, where it runs `forgetKeys` and sets the `off/revoked` status instead of retrying. A wiped hub answers 401 for an unknown signer, so the shared check doesn't misfire on F-003's scenario.
+The hub's `pull` reply carries the key record's `version` (it already bumps on every ring append); the session keeps the version its ring came from, and a pull answering a higher one reloads the ring (`reloaded`) before the next seal, so every running device switches within one 25-second poll. **Your call:** this is worth doing only if revocation stays cryptographic under the call in F-008.

-##### F-015 · Typing in a table cell re-reads the whole table as Markdown on every keystroke, and big tables lag.
+#### F-002 • A misbehaving sync hub can crash the app by sending an enormous reply.
 
-> **Area:** MarkdownPM · **Lens:** Hot Path · **Weight:** Medium · **Size:** M · **Net:** +3 · **Origin:** Residue
-
-**Finding**
-
-Every character typed into a table cell makes the editor re-check the entire table by running the full Markdown parser over it, and the parse grows faster than the table. Typing unique text mid-table measured `rescan` at 27.8 ms for 200 rows and 256 ms for 1,000, with micromark alone at 12.7 and 134 ms, which is visible lag. The incremental scan re-reads only the lines around an edit, but `quietAt` accepts only the line above a blank, a heading, a break, or a list line, so a table row is never a place to stop: `rescan` widens to the whole table, and `tableRegions` grabs the contiguous non-blank block and confirms it with `isTable`, one parse of all its text, shrinking line by line while that parse fails. `isTable` remembers results by text through `perText`, and its own comment notes that a table being typed in mints one entry per keystroke, so every keystroke misses. `CellEditor`'s listener commits each cell keystroke into the page, which steps the scan.[^15]
+| Concern | Scale | Origin | Base | Date |
+|---------|-------|--------|------|------|
+| Low | Small (=🟢+5=) | Shortcut | `f6511401d` | **Created:** 09-23-2026<br>**Updated:** 10-03-2026 |
 
-**Fix | Literal**
+**Description**
 
-`regions.ts` keeps the two-line `isTable` parse that confirms header plus delimiter, then extends the body line by line through `endsBody`: a blank line ends it, and a line that passes the lexical prefilter `MAY_OPEN` (a superset of every block opener's first characters) ends it when `opensBlock`, one parse of `| a |\n| - |\n<line>` remembered per line through `perText` at a cap of 4096, yields more than one block. The whole-block confirm and the shrink loop are deleted. This is the prefilter-then-cached-parse pattern `isHeadingLine` and `isThematicBreakLine` already follow; per-line facts the scan holds can't answer it, since `tableRegions` runs before the scan derives headings, quotes, breaks, and references, and the facts it derives later differ from the table extension for an unpaired fence, a `*` item, a bare `-` or `1.`, a `<span>`-led row, a footnote definition, and indented code. Table extents don't change. The `rescan` window still spans the table, so what remains per keystroke is the linear line scan with no micromark parse: 0.3 ms at 200 rows and about 2 ms at 1,000, and a cold open of a 1,000-row table whose every row is digit-led and unique, the worst case, costs about 80 ms once. HEAD's whole-table parse also throws under the development export condition (a `devlop` assertion in `mdast-util-gfm-task-list-item`) on a body holding an empty list item followed by a `[ ] task` line, which crashes `scanDoc` in `npm run dev`; the new path never parses two body lines together. A seeded property in `Engine/Tables/regions.test.ts`, `a table body runs exactly as far as the whole-table parse reads it`, checks over 2,000 seeds that each region's text parses as one table and that the region plus its next non-blank line doesn't; reverting `endsBody` to blank-only, or dropping any opener class from `MAY_OPEN`, turns it red within 69 seeds. The property's seeded `stream` generator is the one `Engine/docScan.test.ts` already holds, shared from a test helper rather than copied.
+A sync hub, hostile or broken, can crash the whole app by sending back a reply that never ends. The hub limits the size of every request it accepts, but the app buffers whatever the hub sends back into memory before looking at it, and the transport runs in the Electron main process. An unbounded reply takes the app down, and the session restarts on every launch. `transport.ts:26` collects chunks with `res.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk))` and keeps no running total, and `call.ts:90` casts `JSON.parse(reply.body)` to the route's reply type with no shape check.[^2]
```
